item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"The request supplies that the ebook vanished while the loan was still active; distinguishing that event from a return is a direct conclusion from those facts.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s2","status":"keep","reason":"This defines a return by the ordinary completion or voluntary early termination of a loan and adds no external descriptive premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s3","status":"keep","reason":"The request supplies that the publisher withdrew the ebook after the library loan began and that it vanished during that loan, which entails loss of access before the loan's expected end.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes an unsupported general claim about a necessary condition for library lending.","claims":[{"claim":"Library lending depends on borrowers having predictable access to loaned materials.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that predictable access is necessary to library lending generally?"}]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence describes general institutional practices and common licensing restrictions that the request does not supply.","claims":[{"claim":"Libraries generally acquire rights that authorize them to lend ebooks.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How are public-library ebook lending rights ordinarily acquired and structured?"},{"claim":"Library ebook lending rights are often limited by time, price, or circulation conditions.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"How prevalent are time, price, and circulation limits in public-library ebook licenses?"},{"claim":"Libraries place licensed ebook titles in their catalogs and promise borrowers defined loan periods.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do public libraries generally catalog licensed ebooks and commit to defined loan periods at checkout?"}]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The characterization of canceling the supplied active loan is an inference, but the asserted legitimacy of future withdrawal and existence of rights disputes require external support.","claims":[{"claim":"Publishers may legitimately withdraw ebook titles from future public-library loans.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Under what contractual or legal circumstances may publishers withdraw ebooks from future library lending?"},{"claim":"Rights disputes sometimes cause publishers to withdraw ebook titles from library lending.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Are there documented rights disputes that have caused ebook withdrawals from public-library lending?"}]},{"id":"p2s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical classification of the supplied mid-loan removal as repossession rather than borrower-initiated or term-ending return.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts a technical mechanism behind digital library lending that the request does not identify.","claims":[{"claim":"Digital library lending applications control ebook access through licensing controls and account authorization.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What technical controls do digital library lending systems use to grant and revoke ebook access?"}]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence adds unsupported claims about system capabilities, the manner of revocation, and comparative physical constraints.","claims":[{"claim":"Digital library lending systems use the same access-control mechanisms both to enforce due dates and to revoke access immediately.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Can the same technical controls used for ordinary ebook expiration also revoke an active loan immediately?"},{"claim":"Immediate revocation of digital library ebook access can occur without conspicuous notice to the borrower.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Can active ebook access be revoked without a clear contemporaneous notice to the borrower, and how often does that occur?"},{"claim":"Physical lending imposes constraints that make mid-loan seizure more difficult than revoking digital access.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What physical or operational constraints make recovery of a physical library book during an active loan harder than digital revocation?"}]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The trapdoor is a metaphor for the supplied revocation power, but the claim that checkout interfaces can resemble a physical library desk is not supplied.","claims":[{"claim":"Digital library checkout screens may be designed to resemble the experience of checking out material at a physical library desk.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do digital library checkout interfaces use visual or interaction conventions that resemble physical library checkout?"}]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"keep","reason":"This draws a value judgment from the supplied unusual mid-loan disappearance and recommends acknowledging it; it adds no external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts general contractual authority and institutional catalog practices not supplied by the request.","claims":[{"claim":"Publisher contracts can require ebook titles to be withdrawn from new library circulation.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What kinds of publisher contracts require withdrawal of ebooks from new public-library circulation?"},{"claim":"Libraries can update their catalogs in response to a publisher's withdrawal of a title.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Can public libraries remove or revise ebook catalog listings when publishers withdraw titles?"}]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"keep","reason":"This proposes that active loans remain accessible through expiration and expressly states proposed exceptions; it does not claim that current law or practice follows that rule.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a proposed protective rule and a conceptual contrast with revocable permission, based on the supplied ability to terminate access mid-loan.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence recommends disclosure by the library and publisher and specifies what that explanation should contain; it asserts no current practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a demand for a normative boundary between prospective withdrawal and interference with the supplied existing loan.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The demand that digital access honor trust is normative, but the premise that public libraries depend on trust is an unsupported generalization.","claims":[{"claim":"Public libraries depend on public trust to perform their institutional role.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that public trust is necessary to the operation or public role of libraries?"}]}]}
